BURHAN:v2p234/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p234/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p234/r5.claim: The author lists Moses’ plural-form address to Pharaoh’s people as another instance of addressing one person with plural wording.
BURHAN:v2p234/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ ففررت منكم لما خفتكم ﴾

ASAD-NOTES:26:20#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:20#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:20#n11/r1.claim: Asad links Moses’ sudden realization that killing the Egyptian was a grievous sin to 28:15–16 and his note on 28:15.
ASAD-NOTES:26:20#n11/r1.anchor: after having killed the Egyptian, Moses suddenly realized that he had committed a grievous sin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:18/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:18/r3.claim: After hearing that Pharaoh and his people wanted to kill him, Moses fled Egypt in fear to Midian, north of the Gulf of Aqaba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:18/r3.anchor: Mısır’ı terkederek Akabe körfezinin kuzeyindeki Medyen’e gitmişti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:18/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:18/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:18/r4.claim: God later gave Moses knowledge, wisdom, and prophethood, then sent him with his brother Aaron to Pharaoh and his people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:18/r4.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak daha sonra ona ilim, hikmet ve peygamberlik görevi verdi, kardeşi Hârûn’la birlikte Firavun ve kavmine gönderdi.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r5.claim: Moses openly acknowledges killing the Copt; after God's guidance and appointment as messenger, his present status differs entirely from his past, so Pharaoh must hear him without dwelling on the past.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r5.anchor: It is evident from this verse that Moses (sws) openly confessed to the killing of the Copt in the words it mentions.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r7.claim: Prophets are upright before being chosen, but uprightness and intellect cannot by themselves guide a person through life's uncertainties; divine guidance is needed, which Moses calls ḥukm and is discussed at 26:83.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r7.anchor: prophets of God are of upright nature even before they are chosen by God as His envoys. However, mere upright nature and intellect are not enough

BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r3.claim: Moses fled to Midian fearing for his life and fearing they would harm him and punish him beyond what his offense deserved.
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r3.anchor: {لما خفتكم} أن تصيبوني بمضرة وتؤاخذوني بما لا أستحقه بجنايتي

BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r4.claim: God granted Moses knowledge and wisdom when he returned from Midian and made him a messenger to Pharaoh’s people.
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r4.anchor: حين رجعت من مدين. {حكما} أي علما وحكمة {وجعلنى من المرسلين} إليكم.

BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r5.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r5.claim: Fath al-Raḥmān interprets “judgment” as prophethood and being made a messenger as a further rank, since some prophets are not messengers.
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r5.anchor: وفي "فتح الرحمن" : حكما أي نبوة وجعلني من المرسلين درجة ثانية للنبوة فرب نبي ليس برسول.

BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r6.claim: Some Sufi masters say that when God intends to raise someone to a high station, He casts fear on him so he flees from people and God unveils the secrets special to him.
BURSEVI:v6p194#2/r6.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : إن الله تعالى إذا أراد أن يبلغ أحدا من خلقه إلى مقام من المقامات العالية يلقي عليه رعبا

QASHANI:26:20-24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:20-24/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:20-24/r2.claim: The wisdom God granted Moses transcends demonstration, acquisition, and reason, and God made him a messenger with it.
QASHANI:26:20-24/r2.anchor: حكمة متعالية عن طريق البرهان وراء طور الكسب والعقل

QASHANI:26:20-24/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:20-24/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:20-24/r8.claim: The passage depicts the veiled self as unable to know the Real, prophetic wisdom, or religious law; it resists obedience, asserts itself, and seeks to overpower revelation.
QASHANI:26:20-24/r8.anchor: وهذه المقالة إشارة إلى أن النفس المحجوبة بمعقولها لا تهتدي إلى معرفة الحق وحكمة الرسالة والشرع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r1.claim: Moses uses plural “you” for fear and flight because he feared Pharaoh and his officials, though he addresses Pharaoh alone in “you claim” and “you enslaved.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r1.anchor: وجمع ضمير الخطاب في منكم وخفتكم بأن كان قد أفرد في: تمنها وعبدت،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r2.claim: Pharaoh's officials had plotted to kill Moses, as also stated in 28:20.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r2.anchor: وهم كانوا قوما يأتمرون لقتله. ألا ترى إلى قوله: إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج .

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r3.claim: The majority parse لما as a particle linking an event with its required consequence according to Sībawayh, or as an adverb meaning “when” according to al-Fārisī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: لما حرف وجوب لوجوب، على قول سيبويه، وظرفا بمعنى حين، على مذهب الفارسي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r4.speaker: حمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r4.claim: A transmission from Ḥamza reads لما with a kasra on the lām and a light mīm, meaning “they frighten you.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة في رواية: لما بكسر اللام وتخفيف الميم، أي يخوفكم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r5.speaker: عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r5.claim: ʿĪsā reads حكم with a ḍamma on the kāf, while the majority use sukūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r5.anchor: وقرأ عيسى: حكما بضم الكاف والجمهور: بالإسكان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r6.claim: حكم means prophethood, and being made one of the messengers is a further rank, since not every prophet is a messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r6.anchor: والحكم: النبوة. وجعلني من المرسلين: درجة ثانية للنبوة، فرب نبي ليس برسول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r7.speaker: وقيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r7.claim: Another gloss takes حكم as knowledge and understanding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r7.anchor: وجعلني من المرسلين: درجة ثانية للنبوة، فرب نبي ليس برسول. وقيل: الحكم: العلم والفهم.

QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r1.claim: Moses’ flight can be read literally as fear for his life; fleeing when one lacks the power to resist is not blameworthy.
QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r1.anchor: يجوز حمله على ظاهره ، وأنه خاف منهم على نفسه

QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r2.claim: Another reading is that Moses feared God’s punishment would descend on them because of their idolatry, or fled in response to Pharaoh’s claim to be their only god.
QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r2.anchor: خفت أن تنزل بكم عقوبة من الله لشؤم شرككم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r1.claim: Moses fled when he feared harm from Pharaoh's people, after being told the council was plotting to kill him; this explains the plural “you.”
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r1.anchor: ففرت ( أي خرجت هاربا ( منكم لما خفتكم ( أي حين توقعت مكروها يصيبني منكم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r2.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r2.claim: Hamza reads لما with kasra on the lām and a light mīm, construing the lām as a preposition and ما as a verbal noun: “because I feared you.”
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة في رواية لما بكسر اللام وتخفيف الميم على أن اللام حرف جر وما مصدرية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r3.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi explains الحكم as prophethood; another explanation is knowledge and understanding of things as they are, with some narrowing that knowledge to what is distinctive of prophethood.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r3.anchor: فوهب لي ربي حكما ( أي نبوة أو علما وفهما للاشياء على ما هي عليه والاول مروي عن السدي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r4.claim: On the prophethood interpretation, making Moses one of the messengers marks God's further favor of the higher rank of messengership.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r4.anchor: اشارة على ظاهر الأول من تفسيري الحكم إلى تفضله تعالى عليه برتبة هي فوق رتبة النبوة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r5.claim: Moses answers that the killing preceded his mission and was unintended, since the blow was meant as discipline; he then turns back to Pharaoh's boast of raising him.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r5.anchor: من نسبة القتل إلى مسلم لكنه ليس مما أوبخ به ويقدح في نبوتي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r6.claim: Calling messengership an established divine practice magnifies its office and tells Pharaoh that Moses' mission is no novelty.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#2/r6.anchor: وتنبيها لفرعون على أن رسالته عليه السلام ليس أمرا مبتدعا بل هو مما جرت به سنة الله تعالى شأنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r1.claim: Moses fled from Egypt to Midian because he feared Pharaoh’s people.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r2.claim: God granted Moses judgment, meaning prophethood.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r3.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r3.claim: Muqātil instead interprets judgment as knowledge and understanding.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r4.claim: God also made Moses one of the messengers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r9.claim: Moses fled from them out of fear; God then gave him wisdom and made him a messenger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r9.anchor: ففررت منكم لما خفتكم فوهب لي ربي حكما

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r10.claim: Mentioning his wisdom and messengership first answers Pharaoh's attempt to discredit his prophethood through the killing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r10.anchor: رد أولا بذلك ما وبخه به قدحا في نبوته

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r11.claim: Moses does not explicitly deny the upbringing because it is true and does not disprove his claim; he shows it was actually a calamity caused by Israelite enslavement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:19-21/r11.anchor: ولم يصرح برده لأنه كان صدقا غير قادح في دعواه

SULAMI:v2p72#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r1.claim: Fleeing what cannot be endured is among the conduct of messengers, as Moses fled from those he feared.
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم الفرار مما لا يطاق من بين المرسلين قال الله عز وجل : ^ ( وفررت منكم لما خفتكم ) ^

SULAMI:v2p72#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r2.claim: Whoever fears God is made feared by everything, while whoever does not fear God is made to fear everything.
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : من خاف الله ، اخاف الله منه كل شيء ، ومن لم يخف الله أخافه الله من كل شيء

SULAMI:v2p72#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r3.claim: Moses fled Pharaoh's company because he feared their boldness toward God, their failure to honor the messengers, and their lack of signs of divine favor.
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : ففررت من مجاورتكم وخفت من جرأتكم على ربكم لما لم تحفظوا حقوق الرسل

SULAMI:v2p72#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r4.claim: Another gloss says Moses fled because he feared punishment descending on them.
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : فررت منكم لما خفت نزول العذاب عليك

SULAMI:v2p72#5/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r5.claim: A believer should flee with his religion to safety when it is threatened; safety is any place where religion is protected from desire, innovation, and misguidance.
SULAMI:v2p72#5/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : المؤمن يفر بدينه من موضع إلى موضع إذا خاف على دينه فر به إلى مأمن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r6.claim: Moses fled Pharaoh's force and the people who would incite him, fearing execution for the killing, though the deed was accidental and the victim's blood was legally permissible.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r6.anchor: على نفسي أن تقتلوني بذلك القتيل الذي قتلته خطأ

BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r7.claim: God gave Moses wisdom, practical knowledge fit for wise judges, and made him a messenger; he now fears neither death nor anything else from Pharaoh.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r7.anchor: اي علما أعمل به عمل الحكام الحكماء

DURR-FULL:v6p291/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p291/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p291/r8.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the judgment granted to Moses as prophethood.
DURR-FULL:v6p291/r8.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {فوهب لي ربي حكما} قال: النبوة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explains the “judgment” God gave Moses as prophethood.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755/r1.anchor: عن السدى قوله ففررت منكم لما خفتكم فوهب لي ربي حكما والحكم النبوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p114/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p114/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p114/r5.claim: The escape is followed by God correcting, teaching, guiding, and commissioning Moses; this is purposeful explanation, since a person's present state and final outcome matter more than his past.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p114/r5.anchor: فليس ذلك من موسى مجرد إطناب بل لأنه يفيد معنى أن الإنسان ابن يومه لا ابن أمسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r1.claim: ففررت منكم means Moses began fleeing away from Pharaoh and his people, who caused his flight; an implicit noun makes it ‘from fear of you,’ and they had conspired to kill him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r1.anchor: وقوله : { ففررت منكم } أي فرارا مبتدئا منكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r2.claim: حكما means wisdom and knowledge, here Moses's prophethood, beginning when God spoke to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r2.anchor: وأراد بها النبوءة وهي الدرجة الأولى حين كلمه ربه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r3.claim: Moses became a messenger after God showed him the sign, chose him, and commanded him to go to Pharaoh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r3.anchor: أرسله بقوله : { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r6.claim: Ḥukman means prophethood and its wisdom; ʿĪsā reads ḥukuman with ḍamma on both ḥāʾ and kāf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r6.anchor: وقوله حكما يريد النبوة وحكمتها، وقرأ عيسى «حكما» بضم الحاء والكاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r7.claim: Being made a messenger is a further rank beyond prophethood, since some prophets are not messengers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r7.anchor: وقوله وجعلني من المرسلين درجة ثانية للنبوة فرب نبي ليس برسول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r1.claim: Moses fled from them to Midian because he feared for his life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r1.anchor: ففررت منكم أي ذهبت من بينكم لما خفتكم على نفسي إلى مدين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r2.speaker: عاصم الجحدري والضحاك وابن يعمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r2.claim: They read لَمَّا with kasra on the lām and a light mīm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم الجحدري والضحاك وابن يعمر لما بكسر اللام وتخفيف الميم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r3.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r3.claim: One interpretation of the wisdom God granted Moses is prophethood.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p119#5/r4.claim: A second interpretation of the granted wisdom is knowledge and understanding.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137#3/r4.claim: Moses says the earlier situation has ended: God has now sent him, so obedience brings safety and defiance brings ruin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137#3/r4.anchor: فإن أطعته سلمت، وإن خالفته عطبت.

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r1.claim: Flight and escape are synonymous terms; gift, connection, and donation are likewise synonyms.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r1.anchor: الفرار والهرب من النظائر، والهبة والصلة والعطية من النظائر

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r2.claim: A gift is a legally valid contract by offer and acceptance according to consensus.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r2.anchor: الهبة: عقد جائز في الشرع صحتها بالإيجاب والقبول بالاتفاق

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r3.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r3.claim: Most jurists require taking possession and delivery for a gift to become valid.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r3.anchor: قيل: بالقبض والتسليم عند أكثر الفقهاء

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r4.speaker: الهادي
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r4.claim: Al-Hadi holds that a gift is valid without possession.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r4.anchor: وقال الهادي: تصح من غير قبض

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r5.speaker: أهل العراق
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r5.claim: The Iraqi jurists do not permit gifting an undivided share when the property is divisible.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r5.anchor: فلا يجوز في المشاع فيما ينقسم عند أهل العراق

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r6.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r6.claim: Al-Shafiʿi holds that such a gift is valid.

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r12.claim: Moses fled to Midian because he feared Pharaoh's people would kill him over the Egyptian he struck.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r12.anchor: ففررت منكم إلى مدين لما خفتكم على نفسي من القتل بالقبطي

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r13.claim: Another explanation is that Moses feared their reaction to his religious dissent and aid to the Israelites.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r13.anchor: خفتكم لما ظهر مني من مخالفتكم في الدين وإعانتي بني إسرائيل

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r14.claim: One view denies retaliation because Moses acted mistakenly.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r14.anchor: قيل: لم يكن عليه قصاص؛ لأنه مخطئ

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r15.claim: A second view denies retaliation because the Egyptian's blood was licit.

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r16.claim: A third view says retaliation was a legal institution not yet established, so Moses feared oppression and transgression.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r16.anchor: القصاص أمر شرعي؛ ولم يكن ثم شرع، وإنما خاف منهم الظلم والتعدي

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r17.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r17.claim: Ḥukm means knowledge and understanding; the author prefers this because it is paired with messengerhood.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r17.anchor: قيل: علما وفهما؛ وهو الأولى؛ لأنه عطفه على الرسالة

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r18.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r18.claim: Another interpretation of ḥukm is prophethood.

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r19.claim: Being made one of the messengers means being included among the prophets.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r19.anchor: وجعلني من المرسلين أي: من جملة الأنبياء

JISHUMI:v7p5350/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5350/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5350/r1.claim: Moses fled before his prophethood, became a prophet after leaving Egypt, and struck the Egyptian before prophethood.
JISHUMI:v7p5350/r1.anchor: أن فراره كان قبل النبوة، وأن نبوته كانت بعد خروجه من مصر

JISHUMI:v7p5350/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5350/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5350/r2.claim: The phrase “my Lord gave me” knowledge shows that all knowledge comes from God: necessary knowledge is created by Him; acquired knowledge follows His proofs, reason, and prompting; revealed knowledge comes by His revelation.

MUQATIL:26:19-22/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:19-22/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:19-22/r3.claim: Moses fled to Midian because he feared they would kill him; God gave him knowledge and understanding and made him a messenger to them.
MUQATIL:26:19-22/r3.anchor: { ففررت منكم } إلى مدين { لما خفتكم } أن تقتلون { فوهب لي ربي حكما } يعنى العلم والفهم { وجعلني من المرسلين } [آية: 21] إليكم.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#3/r1.claim: Moses fled to Midian because he feared they would kill him, after a believer from Pharaoh's family warned that the officials were plotting his death and told him to leave.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#3/r1.anchor: إلى مدين ﴿ لما خفتكم ﴾ أن تقتلونى وذلك حين قال له مؤمن من آل فرعون ان الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج الآية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#3/r2.claim: God gave Moses prophethood and knowledge, removing his ignorance and error, and made him one of the messengers.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#3/r2.anchor: فوهب لي ربي حكما ﴾ نبوة وعلما فزال عنى الجهل والضلالة ﴿ وجعلني من المرسلين ﴾ من جملة رسله

QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r14.claim: Moses fled to Midian when he feared Pharaoh’s people after the killing, as also related in 28:21.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r14.anchor: أي خرجت من بينكم إلى مدين كما في سورة «القصص»

QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r15.speaker: السدي وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r15.claim: They interpret the حكم God gave Moses as prophethood.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r16.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r16.claim: He interprets it as teaching the Torah, which contains God’s law.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r16.anchor: الزجاج: تعليم التوراة التي فيها حكم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r17.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r17.claim: Another interpretation is that حكم means knowledge and understanding.

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r4.claim: Moses says his flight followed Pharaoh’s threat after the chiefs plotted to kill him; the threat itself caused his fear and flight.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r4.anchor: ومع ذلك فررت منكم عند قولكم : { إن الملا يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك }

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r5.claim: Thus Pharaoh had no favor concerning the killing: his conduct was closer to wrongdoing because he frightened Moses into fleeing.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r5.anchor: فبين بذلك أنه لا نعمة له عليه في باب تلك الفعلة

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r6.claim: After Moses fled, God benefited him by granting judgment and making him a messenger, while Pharaoh had wronged him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r6.anchor: ثم بين نعمة الله تعالى عليه بعد الفرار ، فكأنه قال أسأتم وأحسن الله إلي

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r7.claim: Razi prefers that ‘judgment’ means knowledge rather than prophethood, since prophethood is separately stated in the next clause.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r7.anchor: والأقرب أنه غير النبوة لأن المعطوف غير المعطوف عليه

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r8.claim: The knowledge intended includes reason, judgment, and religious knowledge of divine unity; God would not send Moses without these perfections.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r8.anchor: فالمراد بالحكم العلم ويدخل في العلم العقل والرأي والعلم بالدين الذي هو التوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r9.claim: The verb ‘bestowed’ expressly indicates that God created this judgment in Moses.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r9.anchor: وقوله : { فوهب لى ربى حكما } كالتنصيص على أن ذلك الحكم من خلق الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r10.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r10.claim: The Muʿtazilites interpret the judgment as divine graces (luṭf); Razi calls this very weak because grace is given to all without withholding, so its specification needs a reason.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r10.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : المراد منه الألطاف وهو ضعيف جدا لأن الألطاف مفعولة في حق الكل

RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r4.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains the plural ‘from you’ and ‘I feared you’ as including Pharaoh and the chiefs who plotted, while the singular favor and enslavement refer to Pharaoh alone.
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r4.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) إنما جمع الضمير في { منكم } و { خفتكم } مع إفراده

STUDYQURAN:26:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:21/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:21/r1.claim: Moses’ flight was to Midian, as narrated at 28:21–22.
STUDYQURAN:26:21/r1.anchor: This verse refers to Moses’ flight to Midian

STUDYQURAN:26:21/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:21/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:21/r2.claim: Ḥukm, rendered judgment, can also mean decision-making power; some commentators understand it as knowledge, intelligence, or understanding rather than prophethood.
STUDYQURAN:26:21/r2.anchor: Judgment renders ḥukm, a word that can also mean “power” in the sense of power to make a decision

STUDYQURAN:26:21/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:21/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:26:21/r3.claim: Some interpret the granted ḥukm as knowledge, intelligence, or understanding rather than prophethood.
STUDYQURAN:26:21/r3.anchor: some commentators understand it to mean something other than prophethood

TAB-FULL:v17p559/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p559/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v17p559/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explicitly identifies the bestowed judgment as prophethood.
TAB-FULL:v17p559/r1.anchor: عن السدي: " {فوهب لي ربي حكما} [الشعراء: 21] والحكم: النبوة "

SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r1.claim: The common reading doubles the mīm in lammā; Sibawayh calls it a particle of occurrence, while al-Fārisī takes it as meaning when.
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r1.anchor: العامة على تشديد الميم وهي " لما " التي هي حرف وجوب عند سيبويه أو بمعنى حين عند الفارسي.

SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r2.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r2.claim: Hamza reads with kasra on the lām and a light mīm, meaning because I feared you.
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r2.anchor: وروي عن حمزة بكسر اللام وتخفيف الميم أي: لتخوفي منكم.

SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r3.claim: On Hamza's reading, mā is a verbal noun marker; this resembles his reading of 3:81, discussed earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r3.anchor: و " ما " مصدرية. وهذه القراءة تشبه قراءته في آل عمران: " لما آتيتكم "

SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r4.speaker: عيسى
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r4.claim: Isa reads ḥukman with a ḍamma on the kāf by vowel assimilation.
SAMIN-DURR:26:21/r4.anchor: وقرأ عيسى " حكما " بضم الكاف إتباعا.

TABATABAI:26:21/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:21/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:21/r8.claim: Moses fled after the killing because a man warned him that Pharaoh's council was plotting to kill him; he left the city afraid and watchful, as described in 28:20–21.
TABATABAI:26:21/r8.anchor: وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى قال يا موسى إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين فخرج منها خائفا يترقب

TABATABAI:26:21/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:21/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:21/r9.claim: Here ḥukm means sound insight into reality and skillful judgment in applying it to action.
TABATABAI:26:21/r9.anchor: وأما الحكم فالمراد به - كما استظهرناه - إصابة النظر في حقيقة الأمر وإتقان الرأي في العمل به

TABATABAI:26:10-68/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r1.claim: The ḥukm given after the killing and the ḥukm and knowledge given before it in 28:14 can be distinct levels: Moses received increasing degrees before the killing, after fleeing, and after Pharaoh drowned, culminating in the Torah, which contains God's judgment.
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r1.anchor: إنما ورد لفظ الحكم ها هنا وفي سورة القصص منكرا وهو مشعر بمغايرة كل منهما الآخر وقد ورد في خصوص التوراة أنها متضمنة للحكم

TABATABAI:26:10-68/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r2.claim: The staged gift of ḥukm is like natural soundness in childhood followed by mature reasoning and management; these qualities belong to one kind that grows over time.
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r2.anchor: نظير ما يرزق بعض الناس أوان صباه سلامة في فطرته قلما يميل معها طبعه إلى الشر والفساد ثم إذا نشأ يعطي اعتدالا في التعقل وجودة في التدبير

TABATABAI:26:10-68/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r3.claim: Tabataba'i rejects defining ḥukm as prophethood because neither the wording nor the context supports it.
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r3.anchor: عدم استقامة تفسير بعضهم الحكم بالنبوة لعدم دليل عليه من جهة اللفظ ولا المقام

TABATABAI:26:10-68/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r4.claim: The Qur'an distinguishes judgment from prophethood by naming them separately alongside the Book, as in 3:79, 6:89, and 45:16.
TABATABAI:26:10-68/r4.anchor: ذكر الحكم والنبوة في مواضع من كلامه وفرق بينهما كقوله أن يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة

TABATABAI:26:21-22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r1.claim: Moses' claim to be made a messenger answers Pharaoh's disbelief in the mission because of his prior familiarity with Moses; that inference would hold only for an acquired, predictable status, whereas mission is a divine gift.
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r1.anchor: استغرابهم واستبعادهم رسالته استنادا إلى سابق معرفتهم بحاله إنما يستقيم لو كانت الرسالة أمرا اكتسابيا يمكن أن يحدس به أو يتوقع حصوله

TABATABAI:26:21-22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r2.claim: God made Moses a messenger by gift, just as He gave him judgment without acquisition.
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r2.anchor: بل هي أمر وهبي لا تأثير للأسباب العادية فيها وقد جعله الله من المرسلين كما وهب له الحكم بغير اكتساب

ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r1.claim: The حكم God gave Moses means the Torah, which contains God’s legal judgments.
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r1.anchor: يعنى التوراة التي فيها حكم الله

TABRISI:26:20-25/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:20-25/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:20-25/r7.claim: God granted Moses judgment, meaning prophethood.
TABRISI:26:20-25/r7.anchor: { فوهب لي ربي حكما } أي نبوة

TABRISI:26:20-25/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:20-25/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:26:20-25/r8.claim: Alternatively, judgment is knowledge of what wisdom requires, including the Torah and knowledge of lawful and unlawful matters and other rulings.
TABRISI:26:20-25/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن الحكم العلم بما تدعو إليه الحكمة وهو الذي وهبه الله تعالى لموسى من التوراة والعلم بالحلال والحرام

TABRISI:26:20-25/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:20-25/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:20-25/r9.claim: God made Moses a prophet among the other prophets.

THALABI:v7p161/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p161/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p161/r5.claim: Moses fled to Midian because he feared Pharaoh’s people; God then granted him understanding and knowledge and made him a messenger.
THALABI:v7p161/r5.anchor: ففررت منكم لما خفتكم إلى مدين فوهب لي ربي حكما فهما وعلما وجعلني من المرسلين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r1.claim: Moses says he fled from them to protect himself when he feared them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r1.anchor: أي ذهبت (¬6) من بينكم حذرا # على نفسى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r2.claim: Maqatil says Moses fled to Midian because he feared Pharaoh's people would kill him for the man he had killed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: {ففررت منكم} إلى مدين (¬1) لما خفتكم أن تقتلوني بمن قتلته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi interpret the wisdom God gave Moses as prophethood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r3.anchor: يعني: نبوة. قاله ابن عباس، والسدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r4.claim: Maqatil interprets the wisdom as knowledge and understanding.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the wisdom as intellect.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r6.claim: Al-Farra interprets the wisdom as the Torah, but al-Wahidi rejects this as unlikely because the Torah was given after Pharaoh drowned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p35/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: التوراة (¬5). وهو بعيد؛ لأن التوراة أوتي (¬6) بعد غرق فرعون.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r2.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r2.claim: Al-Suddī explains “I fled from you” as “I escaped from you.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r2.anchor: {ففررت منكم} [الشعراء: 21] تفسير السدي، يعني: فهربت منكم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r3.claim: Moses fled when he feared them as he headed toward Midian.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r3.anchor: {لما خفتكم} [الشعراء: 21] ، يعني: حيث توجه تلقاء مدين.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r4.claim: God granted Moses judgment, meaning prophethood, and made him one of the messengers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r4.anchor: {فوهب لي ربي حكما} [الشعراء: 21] النبوة. {وجعلني من المرسلين} [الشعراء: 21]

BURHAN:v3p6#3/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p6#3/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p6#3/r5.claim: Moses' plural address to Pharaoh's people is included among examples of using plural wording for a singular addressee.
BURHAN:v3p6#3/r5.anchor: ﴿ ففررت منكم لما خفتكم ﴾ 5 وغير ذلك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r1.claim: Firār fundamentally means flight; mafar is the place a fugitive reaches, al-farr are the fleeing people, and farartu ʿan al-amr means I avoided it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r1.anchor: الأصل في الفرار : أنه الهرب . والمفر : المكان الذي ينتهي إليه الفار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r2.claim: The related verb iftarr can describe a man showing his teeth while laughing; a horse’s farāra eye is striking enough to reveal its quality.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r2.anchor: وافتر الرجل ضاحكا ، إذا أبدى أسنانه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r3.claim: Firār can mean fleeing, including escape from death or killing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p463/r3.anchor: أحدها : الهرب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الشعراء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r5.claim: Moses answers Pharaoh's reminder of his upbringing by citing God's gift of judgment and messengership, then overturns Pharaoh's claimed favor by pointing to his enslavement of the Israelites.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r5.anchor: فأقر بذلك موسى وذكر من أمر فراره منهم ما ذكر
